articles.text: Jean and Carmen play tennis at the club. Jean wins both sets 6–1 and 6–2. Bob congratulates Jean and asks her opinion of the courts. Jean says they’re excellent and it’s her first time playing on grass.

Bob tells Jean he has bought tickets for the bullfight this coming Sunday. Jean says she can’t go because she and Bob promised to take the children to the countryside. Bob suggests telling the children they’ll go another day, but Jean insists they can’t break the promise, so Bob tells Jean she’ll have to take them herself because he won’t miss the bullfight for anything.

A reading selection describes the Old Quarter of Las Palmas. The northern part of the city retains its original colonial character with narrow streets and Spanish colonial buildings. The main street is lined with shops selling typical local products, and there’s a large market made up of stalls where locals buy their goods. Although the area looks dirty and old, prices are good and it’s worth shopping there.
